H_hierarchical.evidence: The controller is explicitly two-level: upper signalling states I-IV, with State III containing the sleep/droop/power mode-switch submachine.

G_guards_arith.evidence: Transitions depend on converter role, sending/receiving completion, signal voltage detection, six-bit signal-series fields, conjunctions over ss[1]/ss[3], bus-voltage limits, SoC, and current-amplitude commands.

A_actions_nontrivial.evidence: States send and receive signal series, continuously monitor DC bus voltage, perform current compensation, switch other sources on, set droop/power/sleep modes, set charge/discharge current references, and limit PV power.

F_fault_recovery.evidence: The paper handles planned on-grid/off-grid transfer via an off-signal, but says abrupt grid-converter break/plug-out cannot be actively regulated and falls back only vaguely to restart or all-droop behavior.

T1_cross_section_element.evidence: State hierarchy is in §6.4.2, guard encoding is defined in §6.3/Table 6-1 and Appendix A6, and State IV current-compensation behavior is referenced back to Chapter 4.

T2_implicit_domain_term.evidence: Terms such as droop mode, power mode, MPPT, SoC, plug-and-play, and current compensation carry domain-specific control semantics not fully restated in the state bullets.

T3_implicit_action_from_prose.evidence: Actions are partly narrated outside the state definitions: experiments describe switch-on, charge/discharge current, full-charge sleep return, and PV limitation behavior tied back to modes.

T4_multivar_arith_guard.evidence: The second-level machine uses conjunctions such as ss[1] with ss[3], while the broader controller also tests bus voltage limits, SoC, PV power, and signal-series current bits.

T5_composite_internal_behavior.evidence: Parent State III owns continuous bus-voltage monitoring and sending/receiving triggers while also containing the sleep/droop/power internal state machine.

T6_global_cross_cutting_recovery.evidence: Signal-voltage arrival is handled at the parent State III level, so the receive transition applies across the internal sleep, droop, and power substates.

C1_speculative_dfs.evidence: There is one explicit composite state with role-dependent entry into sleep or droop, but no deep pseudo-state chain.

C2_expr_ir_smt.evidence: The six-bit signal protocol and mode machine create many boolean/comparison guards whose consistency is easier to check with a unified expression IR.

C3_forced_and_aspect.evidence: Parent State III declares continuous monitoring once and signal-arrival handling applies across all three internal modes, matching aspect/forced-transition compression.

C4_abstract_action.evidence: Outputs are mostly concrete power-electronics commands and DC-bus signal-series actions, not channel-agnostic log/publish/notify effects.

key_nl_quotes: The system state machine contains two levels.
sleep mode, droop mode and power mode
one_line_pitch: A two-level converter controller whose parent monitoring state decodes signal-series guards into cross-cutting receiving behavior and concrete mode/current actions.
rationale: This is a strong stress-test because the paper gives an explicit hierarchical state machine with a parent state that owns continuous monitoring and contains a second-level mode machine. The guard/action semantics are distributed across the state-machine section, signal-series table, appendix, and experimental scenarios, creating exactly the kind of context-splitting and semantic attribution that weakens Umple-style baselines. Fault handling is limited, but H/G/A plus BD and FT are high enough for a top candidate.
